([[Chalon-sur-Saône]], France) | college = [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] (2023–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 24 | draft_team = [[New York Knicks]] | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = 2022–2023 | team1 = [[Élan Chalon]] | years2 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–present | team2 = [[Washington Wizards]] | highlights = }} '''Kyshawn Shanty Alonzo George''' (born 12 December 2003) is a Swiss-Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]]. ==Early life and career== George was born on 12 December 2003 and grew up in [[Monthey]], Switzerland.{{Cite web |date=16 June 2023 |title=Kyshawn George |url=https://miamihurricanes.com/roster/kyshawn-george/ |access-date=30 December 2024 |publisher=[[Miami Hurricanes]]}} His father, Deon George, was born and raised in Montreal, Canada, and played professional basketball in Switzerland.{{cite web |last1=Chidley-Hill |first1=John |title=George ready for “hometown” NBA debut {{!}} Globalnews.ca |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/10796562/george-ready-for-hometown-nba-debut/ |website=Global News |agency=The Canadian Press|access-date=25 May 2026 |language=en |date=October 5, 2024}}{{cite web |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |title=Versatile Swiss guard Kyshawn George (Class of '23) signs with University of Miami |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/versatile-swiss-guard-kyshawn-george-030350732.html |website=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |access-date=27 February 2024 |date=20 April 2023}} George was part of the team that won the Swiss U16 basketball championship in 2016.{{Cite web |last=Benjamin |first=Marcus |date=20 April 2023 |title=Men's BB: Miami lands commitment from Kyshawn George |url=https://miami.rivals.com/news/men-s-bb-miami-lands-commitment-from-kyshawn-george |website=[[Rivals.com]]}} He later moved to France and played four years with the club [[Élan Chalon]].{{Cite web|url=https://woofradio.net/miami-freshman-guard-kyshawn-george-seizing-opportunity-with-louisville-up-next-tonight-its-just-me-getting-confidence-in-the-team/|publisher=[[WOOF (AM)|WOOF]]|title=Miami freshman guard Kyshawn George seizing opportunity with Louisville up next tonight: "It's just me getting confidence in the team"|date=January 2024}}{{Cite news |date=16 January 2024 |title=Kyshawn George gagne en responsabilités, Jermaine Love efficace |trans-title=Kyshawn George gains responsibilities, Jermaine Love efficient |url=https://www.lejsl.com/sport/2024/01/16/kyshawn-george-gagne-en-responsabilites-jermaine-love-efficace |access-date=30 December 2024 |newspaper=[[Le Journal de Saône-et-Loire]] |language=fr}} George played mainly for the U18 team from 2019–20 to 2020–21 before then playing for the U21 team in 2021–22 and 2022–23, also spending time with the first-team squad in his last season. He averaged 11.1 points and two rebounds per game in 2021–22 and had 17.6 points, 6.5 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 2.4 steals per game with the team in 2022–23, being named first-team All-U21 Espoir Pro B. With the first team, he averaged 2.9 points and appeared in 16 games in 2022–23.{{Cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=21 April 2023 |title=Versatile Swiss guard added to UM's '23 recruiting class |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-miami-herald/141062929/ |newspaper=[[The Miami Herald]] |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}} George attended Lycée Emiland Gauthey in [[Chalon-sur-Saône]], France. He had a growth spurt in high school, going from a height of {{convert|5|ft|8|in}} to {{convert|6|ft|5|in}} and {{convert|6|ft|7|in}} by the time he entered college.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-miami-herald/141061246/|newspaper=[[The Miami Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=10 January 2024|page=A22|title=Swiss import makes quick impact as first-year guard for Hurricanes}} {{Open access}} He committed to playing [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] in April 2023, being ranked a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]].{{Cite magazine |last=Smith |first=Brian |date=20 April 2023 |title=Canes Hoops Lands Recruit From Switzerland |url=https://www.si.com/college/miami/basketball/canes-hoops-lands-recruit-from-switzerland |access-date=30 December 2024 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}{{Cite magazine |last=Willerup |first=Liam |date=28 January 2024 |title=It's Time To Buy Your Stock In Miami's Kyshawn George |url=https://www.si.com/college/miami/basketball/its-time-to-buy-your-stock-in-miamis-kyshawn-george |access-date=30 December 2024 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}{{Cite news |last=Délèze |first=Adrien |date=27 April 2023 |title=Basket: le Montheysan Kyshawn George fait un pas de plus vers son rêve de NBA |trans-title=Basketball: Montheysan Kyshawn George takes another step towards his NBA dream |url=https://www.lenouvelliste.ch/valais/chablais-valaisan/monthey-district/monthey-commune/basket-le-montheysan-kyshawn-george-fait-un-pas-de-plus-vers-son-reve-de-nba-1283551 |url-access=subscription |access-date=30 December 2024 |newspaper=[[Le Nouvelliste (Valais)|Le Nouvelliste]] |language=fr}} ==College career== Initially a backup, George became a starter midway through his [[freshman]] season at Miami due to injuries. He soon became a top player and received attention as a potential [[2024 NBA draft]] prospect.{{Cite web |last=Stock |first=Christopher |date=29 January 2024 |title='He's a matchup problem': Freshman Kyshawn George impressing coaches, NBA scouts |url=https://247sports.com/college/miami/article/hes-a-matchup-problem-miami-hurricanes-basketball-freshman-kyshawn-george-impressing-coaches-nba-scouts-226346145/ |access-date=30 December 2024 |website=[[247Sports]]}}{{Cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=29 January 2024 |title=UM freshman Kyshawn George on NBA radar as Hurricanes play NC State on road Tuesday |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article284813491.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=30 December 2024 |newspaper=[[The Miami Herald]]}} Following his freshman season, he declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] and received a green room invite.{{Cite web |last=Kirschenbaum |first=Alex |date=14 June 2024 |title=Several More Players Invited To Green Room For 2024 Draft |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/06/six-more-players-invited-to-green-room-for-2024-draft.html |access-date=30 December 2024 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US}} ==Professional career== On June 26, 2024, George was selected with the 24th overall pick by the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]; however, immediately on draft night, he was traded for the 26th and 51st overall picks in the 2024 draft.{{cite web|title=2024 NBA Draft: New York Knicks Acquire Six Draft Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-acquire-six-draft-picks|website=NBA.com|date=26 June 2024|access-date=27 June 2024}} On July 6, he signed with the Wizards.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Wizards Sign First-Rounders Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/wizards-sign-first-rounders-alex-sarr-kyshawn-george.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=6 July 2024|access-date=14 July 2024}} He played his first NBA game on October 24, in a game against the [[2024–25 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=Kyshawn George 2024-25 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/georgky01/gamelog/2025|website=basketball-reference.com|date=18 March 2025|access-date=18 March 2025}} George made his 100th three-pointer on his 59th game on March 13, 2025, marking the fastest a Wizards rookie has hit that milestone. Previously, [[Bradley Beal]] held that record with 100 threes made in 60 games.{{cite web|title=Wizards Rookie Breaks Franchise Record in Recent Win|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/wizards-rookie-breaks-franchise-record-in-recent-win/ar-AA1AWKLl?apiversion=v2&noservercache=1&domshim=1&renderwebcomponents=1&wcseo=1&batchservertelemetry=1&noservertelemetry=1|website=msn.com|date=14 March 2025|access-date=19 March 2025}} George also holds the franchise record of most consecutive games with a made three-pointer by a rookie, with 31. The previous record was held by [[Corey Kispert]], with 15.{{cite web |last=Salao |first=Renzo Pocholo |date=4 March 2025 |title=Wizards: Three Huge Reasons Kyshawn George Is D.C.'s Most Promising Rookie |url=https://athlonsports.com/nba/washington-wizards/wizards-three-reasons-kyshawn-george-best-rookie |access-date=19 March 2025 |website=athlonsports.com}}{{cite web|title=Kyshawn George 2024-25 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/georgky01/gamelog/2025|website=basketball-reference.com|date=24 March 2025|access-date=24 March 2025}} In 68 appearances (38 starts) for Washington during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], he averaged 8.7 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 2.5 assists. On October 24, 2025, George scored a career-high 34 points on 11-of-15 shooting in a victory over the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]]; he also recorded 11 rebounds, four assists, two steals, and three blocks in the game.{{Cite web|title=Breaking down George's historic stats vs. Mavs|url=https://www.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/article/kyshawn-george-puts-up-historic-numbers-vs-mavs|access-date=December 26, 2025|website=monumentalsportsnetwork.com|language=en}} He made 48 starts for the Wizards during the regular season, recording averages of 14.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 4.5 assists. On March 4, 2026, George was diagnosed with a partial tear of the [[ulnar collateral ligament of elbow joint|ulnar collateral ligament]] in his left elbow.{{Cite web|title=Wizards’ Kyshawn George (elbow) out at least 3 weeks|url=https://www.nba.com/news/wizards-kyshawn-george-elbow-injury|access-date=April 26, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} On April 2, Washington confirmed that George would miss the remainder of the year due to the injury.{{Cite web|title=Kyshawn George to miss remainder of season with partial UCL tear|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/kyshawn-george-miss-remainder-season-165715771.html|access-date=April 26, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} == National career == George plays for
